question: Xi Jinping out before 2027?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if China's General Secretary of the Communist Party, Xi Jinping, is removed from power for any length of time between July 3, 2025, and December 31, 2026, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

CCP General Secretary Xi Jinping will be considered removed from power if he announces his resignation from his role as General Secretary, or is otherwise dismissed, detained, disqualified, or otherwise loses his position or is prevented from fulfilling his duties as General Secretary within this market's timeframe.

The primary resolution source for this market will be a consensus of credible reporting.

eventMetadata.context_description: Xi Jinping’s centralized authority within the Chinese Communist Party, reinforced by sustained anti-corruption campaigns that have sidelined potential rivals in military and senior party ranks, underpins the 95.3% trader consensus that he will remain in power through the end of 2026. With no designated successor and generational turnover norms already set aside after his third term, the 21st Party Congress in 2027 is viewed as the likely setting for a fourth term rather than a transition. Continued public appearances and policy continuity through mid-2026 reflect stable elite alignment. Low-probability developments that could still alter the outcome before year-end include abrupt health events, severe economic setbacks, or unexpected fractures in party or military institutions.
